acceptance.given: A skill processes content supplied from an untrusted source under the skill's configured input contract.

oracle.expected: The skill declaration and its validation artifact identify the consumed untrusted content as data-only, with no instruction authority granted.
forbidden: The declaration omits the data-only role.
The untrusted content is treated as executable instruction or authority.
oracle.observable: Static inspection of the skill declaration and validator fixture output during governance validation.

acceptance.then: The declaration explicitly labels the consumed untrusted content as data-only.
acceptance.when: The skill authoring standard and package validator evaluate the untrusted-content declaration.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the untrusted-content declaration validation case where the data-only role is omitted or an instruction-bearing role is declared.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate that every consumed untrusted content source is declared data-only and cannot supply instruction authority.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing skill contract fixture schema and validation behavior backward compatible; revert only the data-only declaration check if rollback is required.

slice_hint.state_transition: Untrusted-content declaration moves from unclassified input to explicitly data-only input under validator control.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted validator test passes for a valid data-only declaration and fails for a declaration that omits or grants authority to untrusted content.

acceptance.given: Untrusted content is available as input to a skill whose targets, commands, tool permissions, and authority are already fixed by the skill-controlled contract.

oracle.expected: Validation observes that untrusted content cannot expand targets, commands, tool permissions, or authority beyond the preexisting skill-controlled scope.
forbidden: Targets are expanded from untrusted content.
Commands are expanded from untrusted content.
Tool permissions are expanded from untrusted content.
Authority is expanded from untrusted content.
oracle.observable: A negative fixture containing a machine-declared authority override is rejected during package validation, while embedded prose instructions remain inert.

acceptance.then: The boundary check records that all four capability dimensions remain bounded by the preexisting skill-controlled scope.
acceptance.when: The package validator evaluates untrusted-content fixtures and performs the scope-boundary check.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the negative untrusted-content fixture that attempts to override controller authority or expand targets, commands, tool permissions, or authority.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject machine-declared overrides and any derived scope expansion from untrusted content while keeping embedded prose inert.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing fixture contract and reject only unauthorized scope expansion; rollback restores the prior validator implementation without data migration.

slice_hint.state_transition: Untrusted input remains data-only and bounded; attempted scope expansion transitions to a validation failure.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The negative override fixture is rejected and no validated output contains expanded targets, commands, tool permissions, or authority.

acceptance.given: The standard or validator documents guarantees for handling untrusted content and arbitrary prose.

oracle.expected: The documented and emitted claims limit guarantees to bounded data-only handling and do not assert semantic injection-proof behavior for arbitrary prose.
forbidden: A claim states that arbitrary prose is semantically injection-proof.
Validation output presents semantic injection-proof guarantees for arbitrary prose.
oracle.observable: Text and structured validation output inspection during governance/documentation validation.

acceptance.then: The standard and validation output contain no semantic injection-proof claim about arbitrary prose.
acceptance.when: The standard and package-validator claims are reviewed for untrusted-content assurance language.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the documentation or validator-output check that finds an assertion of semantic injection-proof guarantees for arbitrary prose.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Constrain assurance wording and validator claims so arbitrary prose is never represented as semantically injection-proof.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Documentation and claim validation remain schema-compatible; rollback removes only the strengthened claim check.

slice_hint.state_transition: Assurance claims move from potentially absolute prose to bounded, explicitly non-injection-proof wording.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The claim scan rejects any semantic injection-proof assertion and accepts only bounded assurance language.

acceptance.given: A capability performs database writes and its capability contract is authored or validated.

oracle.expected: The capability contract explicitly describes transaction handling and failure behavior for the database-write operation.
forbidden: A database-write capability omits transaction-handling behavior.

acceptance.then: The database-write capability contract contains an explicit transaction-handling declaration.
acceptance.when: The capability contract is authored or validated against the A17 governance rule.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the database-write capability contract case whose transaction-handling field or behavior declaration is absent.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require database-write capability declarations to include explicit transaction-handling behavior.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing capability-contract schema compatibility; rollback only the added transaction-handling validation.
